title: Fleet sync remediates legacy SQLite member ledgers instead of skipping rollup
objective: The Weave /review run exposed that `hf sync --auto` still reports several fleet members (observed: network-control, prompt_hub, lane) as legacy C-SQLite `.handoff/ledger.db` sources and then skips their rollup. That is a remembered manual migration, not fleet automation. Upgrade the handoff kernel so fleet sync/fleet status can safely remediate or produce a first-class migration plan for legacy member ledgers without ever treating unreadable ledgers as empty. The default no-C hf binary must remain no-C; use an explicit legacy-sqlite helper path, controlled rebuild, or generated per-member remediation command, with out-of-tree backups and witness-chain verification before cursor advancement.
acceptance_criteria: `hf sync --auto`/fleet remediation detects legacy SQLite member ledgers as a typed remediable condition, not an opaque warning buried in output.

A fleet-wide remediation path exists: either `hf fleet sync --fix` migrates each legacy member through the legacy-sqlite helper safely, or emits a machine-readable migration plan with exact commands and member paths.
Migration keeps the default hf binary C-free/no-C; any C-SQLite reader is isolated behind the existing `legacy-sqlite` feature or a purpose-built helper.
Each migrated member gets an out-of-tree backup path recorded, the source witness chain re-verified, the redb target re-verified, and the central rollup cursor advances only after verification.
Re-running the remediation is idempotent and never treats a legacy/unreadable ledger as an empty ledger.
Tests cover at least one fixture legacy SQLite member ledger and prove sync/fleet status moves from legacy-blocked to healthy/remediated.
